cust_jane: Hi team — hitting intermittent 502s + spikes on POST /v1/generate from our app. First seen 2026-03-15T15:12:03Z. Request_id: r-20260315-9a7b4c2f. Latency ~3s then 502. Can you look?

support_anna: thanks — can you paste the exact curl you used and confirm the full request_id? also tell us region and sdk version if possible.

cust_jane: here’s the curl we used (token redacted):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-20260315-9a7b4c2f" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"Summarize the attached text...","max_tokens":256}'
```
Response was HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway and body empty. SDK: JS 2.3.1. Region: us-east-1.

support_anna: got it. two quick asks: 1) please generate a debug bundle from the Console -> Support -> Export debug bundle (include "request_id" + "trace_id" + payload) OR run the client debug helper: `rw-support debug --req r-20260315-9a7b4c2f --out ./debug-r2026.tar.gz` 2) can you confirm the timestamp (UTC) of the failing request? you listed 15:12:03Z, is that correct?

cust_jane: timestamp confirmed 2026-03-15T15:12:03Z. I ran the helper and uploaded to our S3: s3://acme-uploads/debug-r2026.tar.gz (sent link in ticket).

logs-bot: automatic lookup: quick search in hot indices returned no hits for request_id r-20260315-9a7b4c2f within last 72h. Suggest running KQL across time window +/-5m around 2026-03-15T15:12:03Z and check archived/cold storage.

ravi_sre: KQL to run in Kibana (adjust time range):
```kql
(request.id: "r-20260315-9a7b4c2f") OR (message: "r-20260315-9a7b4c2f")
```
If no hits, run an index scan against archived blobs (our hot index retention is 30 days; cold/archived kept 365 days). For S3 cold retrieval:
```bash
# list objects for that date/region
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-logs-archive/region=us-east-1/date=2026-03-15/ --profile redwood-support
# download candidate shards and grep for request id
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs-archive/region=us-east-1/date=2026-03-15/shard-00012.gz - | zgrep "r-20260315-9a7b4c2f" -n || true
```
Note: cold retrieval can take a few minutes per shard.

miguel_logs: extra tips: some services rewrite request_id into trace.request_id or x-redwood-req in logs — search those fields too. Use this broader KQL: `trace.request_id: "r-20260315-9a7b4c2f" OR http.request.headers.x-redwood-req: "r-20260315-9a7b4c2f"`
Also if the request came through edge proxy, try searching edge-request-id and upstream_request_id.

cust_jane: ran the KQL across +/-10m, nothing in Kibana. I don’t have direct S3 access — can support fetch cold shards?

support_anna: yes we can. miguel, ravi — can you pull cold shards for 2026-03-15 15:05–15:20 UTC for us-east-1 and grep for r-20260315-9a7b4c2f? If found, include the log lines + surrounding 100 lines in the debug bundle.

miguel_logs: will do. one note about retention: hot (kibana) indexes are 30 days. Cold archive retention policy keeps compressed daily shards for 365d. For privacy we scrub tokens on export; we may need the raw shard to see upstream headers — will request a restricted retrieval. Expected ETA: 2–6h depending on shard size and queue.

eng_oncall: FYI if we find the request, check the serving-runtime trace: batch_id, KV cache hit, and model seq_len. Common cause for 502s at that time was batch overflow due to a sudden traffic bump. If bundle shows sequence length > 2048 with batching enabled, that’s a strong signal.

support_anna: opened infra ticket INF-2026-4387 and attached this thread. miguel, please upload any cold log snippets to the ticket and add exact log paths. I’ll update customer when we have artifacts.

miguel_logs: pulled shard-00012.gz from cold archive and grepped — found 1 hit. Extracted context and appended to internal ticket. Relevant lines:
```
2026-03-15T15:12:02.987Z service=runtime instance=i-07abc... request.id=r-20260315-9a7b4c2f trace.request_id=tr-8f4a model=redwood-v1 seq_len=312 batch.size=64 upstream_status=502 error="upstream: write reset by peer"
```
And following lines show repeated OOM attempts in the same batch and a proxy upstream reset.

support_anna: thanks — we’ll share this with the eng team. Customer, short-term mitigation: can you try calling with max_tokens 128 or set client-side concurrency low to avoid large batches? Also consider pinning to dedicated capacity if you need low variability.

cust_jane: trying reduced tokens now, will monitor. thanks for the quick turnaround.

support_anna: closing loop: INF-2026-4387 created for eng to root cause and propose a fix (possible kernel tuning + batch limits). ETA for next update ~6–8h. If you see more 502s, please re-upload any new debug bundles and include the new request_ids. :thumbsup:
